regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Shared regimen: select the exact indication to view its treatment aim, schedule, evidence and patient service.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with DNA copying and repair. This can stop cancer cells dividing. Normal blood-forming cells can also be affected, and kidney function determines how the medicine is cleared.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Carboplatin is infused on Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. The team selects the dose using the prescribed AUC and kidney function. Treatment continues while helpful and tolerated; there is no fixed breast course length.
key_points: Carboplatin is infused on Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. The team selects the dose using the prescribed AUC and kidney function. Treatment continues while helpful and tolerated; there is no fixed breast course length.
ANC≥1 and platelets≥100 for full dose; ANC<1 or platelets<100 delay.

Blood count, kidney and liver tests are checked before each cycle. The team confirms the kidney-function method, current AUC and previous dose changes. Report numbness, hearing changes, infection and bleeding. Additional tests follow symptoms and the individual plan.

NCCP protocols specify their own AUC4–6 schedules/counts. The linked product SmPC has broader labelled posology with different general count and interval recommendations. It supplements safety review and does not silently replace the exact NCCP thresholds.
HPRA allows possible individual benefit/risk exception below 30 mL/min; NCCP requires extreme caution at>20≤30 and excludes≤20. The proposal does not compute a dose in these bands.
NCCP says no routine hepatic adjustment; significant new/moderate-severe liver injury still requires review under current product safety warnings.
AUC6 q 21 trial, not a q 28 trial, not all AUC4–6 doses.
Biomarker subgroup was small; no individual response guarantee or general benefit for every HRD/gene alteration.
BRCA1 methylation, lowBRCA1 mRNA and highMyriadHRD score did not identify the same carboplatin advantage; do not equate these with germline BRCA1/2 evidence.
Advanced setting, not an adjuvant cure or survival estimate.
Comparative outcomes concern docetaxel monotherapy; not carboplatin combinations, modern immunotherapy, PARP inhibitors or antibody–drug conjugates.
Do not assign breast trial outcomes to gynaecology or head-neck indications.
Trial planned duration and scan schedule must not overwrite the NCCP breast until-progression/toxicity course.
Response rate is tumour shrinkage, not survival or cure.
Dose(mg)=selectedAUC×(verifiedGFR[mL/min]+25)
For Calvert dosing use verified absolute GFR in mL/min, capped at 125 mL/min. Do not substitute indexed laboratory eGFR in mL/min/1.73m².
Extensive prior treatment or qualifying radiotherapy can make Calvert inappropriate under current HPRA safety guidance; obtain specialist dose review.

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Advanced breast cancer disease control
disease_and_biomarker_context: Breast-specific education and trial interpretation; retain all other NCCP source indication codes in the executable protocol.
eligibility_orientation: Metastatic breast cancer; ECOG 0–2. Confirm prior treatment, clinical suitability and local off-label approval/consent.
important_cautions: Carboplatin for metastatic breast cancer is an off-label use under this Irish NCCP protocol. The treating team must explain this, obtain informed consent and follow local Drugs and Therapeutics Committee approval requirements.

Biomarker subgroup was small; no individual response guarantee or general benefit for every HRD/gene alteration.

Advanced setting, not an adjuvant cure or survival estimate.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Carboplatin AUC4–6 · 21-day schedule: High at AUC ≥4
premedication_and_prophylaxis: NCIS Table 1 allows clinician-selected ondansetron splitting to 8 mg twice daily or reduction to 8 mg once daily according to the individual patient.
Review ondansetron QT risk and other QT-prolonging medicines/electrolytes.
Check dexamethasone interactions, diabetes, sleep and infection effects; aprepitant/steroid interaction is already reflected in the specified row.
Review metoclopramide renal function, neurological contraindications, duration and extrapyramidal risk; do not automatically stack with olanzapine.
AUC reduction below 4 requires an individual prophylaxis review; history of emesis and patient factors may justify continuing stronger protection.
No universal G-CSF, antibiotic, antiviral or acid-suppression prescription is stated by the carboplatin protocol. G-CSF requires individual febrile-neutropenia risk review.
Routine hypersensitivity premedication is usually unnecessary, but antiemetic prophylaxis is still required. Prior allergy/desensitisation is a separate specialist plan.
patient_education: Take the prescribed anti-sickness medicines before treatment and on the following days, even if you feel well. Follow your own prescription and contact the team if nausea or vomiting is not controlled.
Keep blood tests and use the emergency contact for fever, chills or bleeding. Preventive growth-factor injections depend on individual risk.
Tell the team about every medicine or supplement, especially treatments that affect kidneys, hearing or bleeding. Follow individual drinking advice.
The anti-sickness plan may affect sleep, glucose and bowel symptoms. Confirm the exact doses and last day of each medicine; contact the team if symptoms persist.
special_support: NCIS Table 1 allows clinician-selected ondansetron splitting to 8 mg twice daily or reduction to 8 mg once daily according to the individual patient.
Review ondansetron QT risk and other QT-prolonging medicines/electrolytes.
Check dexamethasone interactions, diabetes, sleep and infection effects; aprepitant/steroid interaction is already reflected in the specified row.
Review metoclopramide renal function, neurological contraindications, duration and extrapyramidal risk; do not automatically stack with olanzapine.
AUC reduction below 4 requires an individual prophylaxis review; history of emesis and patient factors may justify continuing stronger protection.
No universal G-CSF, antibiotic, antiviral or acid-suppression prescription is stated by the carboplatin protocol. G-CSF requires individual febrile-neutropenia risk review.
Routine hypersensitivity premedication is usually unnecessary, but antiemetic prophylaxis is still required. Prior allergy/desensitisation is a separate specialist plan.
Use the dedicated carboplatin AUC ≥4 row. It does not include routine olanzapine.

baseline: Blood count and kidney/liver blood tests.
Measured isotope GFR preferred; if unavailable use a verified appropriate estimated method.
Review prior platinum, allergies, hearing/nerve symptoms, prior dose reductions, other medicines and pregnancy/fertility issues.
before_each_cycle: Review symptoms, blood count, renal and liver profile.
Confirm current prescribed AUC, renal method and prior dose history.
For Cockcroft–Gault or Wright, creatinine must be obtained within 48 hours of treatment and dose recalculated as required.
For carrying forward an isotope-GFR dose, compare actual current creatinine with the value at measurement; >110% needs renal reassessment consideration.
ongoing: Review numbness, tingling and hearing changes regularly, especially after previous platinum/ototoxic medicines or age>65.
Response scans and examination follow the consultant plan, not a universal interval.
Routine cardiac echo, ECG series, DXA and genomic re-testing are not mandated by these two NCCP monotherapy protocols. Additional tests depend on symptoms, other medicines and clinical risks.
priority_toxicities: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting and fatigue
Kidney, hearing and nerve effects
Infusion allergy, particularly with repeat platinum exposure
Fertility effects and harm to an unborn baby
urgent_review_signals: Contact the oncology emergency service immediately for fever or shaking chills, sudden illness, bleeding, new breathlessness, chest pain or severe allergy. Report reduced urine, hearing changes and new numbness promptly. Do not wait for the next visit.

longitudinal_schedule.note: Milestones are not equal time intervals. Your team books and reviews tests. Blood count, kidney and liver tests are checked before each cycle. The team confirms the kidney-function method, current AUC and previous dose changes. Report numbness, hearing changes, infection and bleeding. Additional tests follow symptoms and the individual plan.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Carboplatin is infused on Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. The team selects the dose using the prescribed AUC and kidney function. Treatment continues while helpful and tolerated; there is no fixed breast course length.
route_and_duration: Carboplatin is given through a vein over about 30 minutes after blood and symptom review and prescribed anti-sickness medicines. The complete appointment takes longer. A cannula or existing line may be used; a port is not automatically required.
practical_workflow: One infusion visit per 21-day cycle plus pre-cycle blood tests and clinical review. Additional tests depend on symptoms and the individual plan.
Your team chooses venous access. A port is optional, requires a separate insertion procedure and later removal; it is not removed after every infusion.
Allow time for blood review, preparation, anti-sickness treatment, the infusion and observation. No take-home infusion pump is part of this regimen.
Keep emergency contacts, medicine lists and the next appointment plan. Report line redness, swelling, leakage, pain or fever promptly.
observation_and_access: One infusion visit per 21-day cycle plus pre-cycle blood tests and clinical review. Additional tests depend on symptoms and the individual plan.

evidence_at_a_glance.population: Advanced measurable TNBC unsuitable for local therapy, or germline BRCA1/2-mutated breast cancer irrespective of ER/PgR/HER2 if otherwise eligible.
evidence_at_a_glance.comparison: Carboplatin AUC6 every 21 days versus docetaxel 100 mg/m² every 21 days
evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: Exact 21-day schedule atAUC6 only; NCCP also permits consultant-selectedAUC4–6.

endpoints.interpretation: No carboplatin superiority in the overall trial population.
endpoints.analysis_status: Published randomized phase III; prespecified biomarker analysis

sources.label: Tutt et al. Carboplatin in BRCA1/2-mutated and triple-negative breast cancer BRCAness subgroups: the TNT Trial. Nature Medicine 2018;24:628–637

endpoints.interpretation: Small subgroup of 43 patients. Response is not cure or survival; other HRD markers did not show the same predictive effect.
endpoints.analysis_status: Published randomized phase III; prespecified biomarker analysis

sources.label: Tutt et al. Carboplatin in BRCA1/2-mutated and triple-negative breast cancer BRCAness subgroups: the TNT Trial. Nature Medicine 2018;24:628–637

evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: The overall comparison showed no response, PFS or OS superiority. The small germline BRCA1/2 subgroup showed greater response and PFS with carboplatin. Overall median OS was 12.8 versus 12.0 months, with no demonstrated advantage (restricted-mean comparison P=.96).
limitations: AUC6 q 21 trial, not a q 28 trial, not all AUC4–6 doses.
Biomarker subgroup was small; no individual response guarantee or general benefit for every HRD/gene alteration.
BRCA1 methylation, lowBRCA1 mRNA and highMyriadHRD score did not identify the same carboplatin advantage; do not equate these with germline BRCA1/2 evidence.
Advanced setting, not an adjuvant cure or survival estimate.
Comparative outcomes concern docetaxel monotherapy; not carboplatin combinations, modern immunotherapy, PARP inhibitors or antibody–drug conjugates.
Do not assign breast trial outcomes to gynaecology or head-neck indications.
Trial planned duration and scan schedule must not overwrite the NCCP breast until-progression/toxicity course.
Response rate is tumour shrinkage, not survival or cure.
Planned crossover to the other study treatment complicates interpretation of overall survival.

context_profiles.component_rationale: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with DNA copying and repair. This can stop cancer cells dividing. Normal blood-forming cells can also be affected, and kidney function determines how the medicine is cleared. Radiotherapy directs radiation at a carefully planned area. It is delivered on its own appointment calendar. Effects depend on which tissues receive radiation and can build up during the course or continue after it finishes.

Radiation has a separate appointment calendar; the team coordinates any interruptions or changes.

Blood cells / infection: Fever, shivering, sudden illness, unusual bruising or bleeding needs prompt oncology advice.

Teeth / jaw / swallowing: Dental review, nutrition and swallowing support continue through recovery. Report jaw stiffness, weight loss or choking.

context_profiles.regimen_role: Nivolumab and ipilimumab for advanced melanoma
context_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab and ipilimumab help immune cells recognise and attack melanoma. The combination phase is followed by nivolumab alone when appropriate. The aim in this setting is to control advanced disease; benefit and toxicity are reviewed for the individual.
context_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00431a: advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults. This patient guide is the melanoma context, not the separate liver-cancer indication.
context_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can reduce T-cell activity. This can help immune cells act against melanoma, but it can also allow inflammation in healthy organs. It is not conventional chemotherapy and side effects can occur even after doses have stopped. Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another checkpoint involved in controlling T cells. Combining it with nivolumab increases immune activity and can increase immune-related toxicity. The four-dose combination phase has a different treatment plan from nivolumab maintenance.
context_profiles.schedule_context: The combination phase gives nivolumab followed by ipilimumab by IV infusion every three weeks for up to four doses. If appropriate, nivolumab alone then continues on the team-selected two-weekly or four-weekly schedule, by the prescribed IV or subcutaneous route. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.
key_points: This is nivolumab1/ipilimumab3, not the lower-ipilimumab combination.
Four induction doses do not mean the whole treatment course is four doses.
Prior immune toxicity and permanent-stop decisions remain relevant when maintenance starts.

context_profiles.regimen_role: Nivolumab and ipilimumab for advanced melanoma
context_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab and ipilimumab help immune cells recognise and attack melanoma. The combination phase is followed by nivolumab alone when appropriate. The aim in this setting is to control advanced disease; benefit and toxicity are reviewed for the individual.
context_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00431a: advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults. This patient guide is the melanoma context, not the separate liver-cancer indication.
context_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can reduce T-cell activity. This can help immune cells act against melanoma, but it can also allow inflammation in healthy organs. It is not conventional chemotherapy and side effects can occur even after doses have stopped. Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another checkpoint involved in controlling T cells. Combining it with nivolumab increases immune activity and can increase immune-related toxicity. The four-dose combination phase has a different treatment plan from nivolumab maintenance.
context_profiles.schedule_context: The combination phase gives nivolumab followed by ipilimumab by IV infusion every three weeks for up to four doses. If appropriate, nivolumab alone then continues on the team-selected two-weekly or four-weekly schedule, by the prescribed IV or subcutaneous route. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.
key_points: This is nivolumab1/ipilimumab3, not the lower-ipilimumab combination.
Four induction doses do not mean the whole treatment course is four doses.
Prior immune toxicity and permanent-stop decisions remain relevant when maintenance starts.
No routine percentage dose reductions: the team may hold or stop immunotherapy and treat the adverse effect.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Shared regimen: select the exact indication to view its treatment aim, schedule, evidence and patient service.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Lung cancer only: first-line metastatic NSCLC or adjuvant NSCLC after surgery and platinum chemotherapy
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Pembrolizumab: Pembrolizumab is an antibody that blocks PD-1, a control switch on immune T cells. Cancer cells can use this switch to reduce immune attack. Blocking it can help the immune system recognise and attack cancer. The same increased immune activity can inflame healthy organs, which is why new symptoms need attention even after treatment ends.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Pembrolizumab 200 mg is given as a drip over about 30 minutes on Day 1 every 3 weeks (21 days). The hospital visit is longer because of checks and preparation. After complete surgery and platinum chemotherapy, the adjuvant course lasts up to 12 months. For metastatic cancer, treatment continues while it remains helpful and tolerable; the team may consider stopping after 24 months of sustained response without progression, or continuing when appropriate.
key_points: Minimal emetic risk; no usual routine premedication.
No pembrolizumab dose reduction; apply specific hold/permanent-stop and restart criteria.
Grade 4/recurrent grade3 generic immune rules have specific endocrine exceptions; controlled hypothyroidism need not interrupt treatment.
Creatinine is ×ULN, never ×baseline; hepatitis and nephritis thresholds must not be confused with stable organ impairment recommendations.
Every-3–6-week thyroid checks continue on both infusion schedules.
Shared clinical protocol; new patient suite is lung-only.

Abnormal liver tests or creatinine do not establish immune causality. Record clinician-assessed hepatitis/nephritis before the definitive source hold/stop pathway; unexplained abnormalities remain a clinical-review decision.

KEYNOTE-091 final OS analysis at ESMO 2026 did not demonstrate a statistically significant OS improvement; chemotherapy-subgroup DFS figures are updated and labelled separately from metastatic KEYNOTE-024.

Requested restart needs documented source-specific recovery, required steroid management/taper and consultant confirmation. Table 1 endocrine exceptions remain separate; existing 12-week failure/taper and permanent-stop criteria retain priority.

For pembrolizumab, grade 2 immune myocarditis, encephalitis or Guillain–Barré syndrome requires withholding and urgent specialist assessment; grades 3–4 require permanent discontinuation. EMA Table 1 separately addresses myocarditis–myositis–myasthenia gravis overlap: use the highest individual CTCAE v4.0 grade; hold grade 2 and permanently stop grades 3–4.

Before requested restart, document whether any previous event met permanent-discontinuation criteria; absent history is not a negative history. Current recovery, steroid taper and consultant confirmation cannot override a prior permanent-stop event. The safety of reinitiating pembrolizumab after immune myocarditis is not established. Preserve the specific controlled-endocrine continuation exceptions.

Shared-protocol eligibility audit now includes head-and-neck, adjuvant RCC, urothelial and cervical maintenance selection. These are distinct from the existing lung, colorectal and melanoma patient-service contexts.

context_profiles.regimen_role: Nivolumab and ipilimumab for advanced melanoma
context_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab and ipilimumab help immune cells recognise and attack melanoma. The combination phase is followed by nivolumab alone when appropriate. The aim in this setting is to control advanced disease; benefit and toxicity are reviewed for the individual.
context_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00431a: advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults. This patient guide is the melanoma context, not the separate liver-cancer indication.
context_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can reduce T-cell activity. This can help immune cells act against melanoma, but it can also allow inflammation in healthy organs. It is not conventional chemotherapy and side effects can occur even after doses have stopped. Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another checkpoint involved in controlling T cells. Combining it with nivolumab increases immune activity and can increase immune-related toxicity. The four-dose combination phase has a different treatment plan from nivolumab maintenance.
context_profiles.schedule_context: The combination phase gives nivolumab followed by ipilimumab by IV infusion every three weeks for up to four doses. If appropriate, nivolumab alone then continues on the team-selected two-weekly or four-weekly schedule, by the prescribed IV or subcutaneous route. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.
key_points: This is nivolumab1/ipilimumab3, not the lower-ipilimumab combination.
Four induction doses do not mean the whole treatment course is four doses.
Prior immune toxicity and permanent-stop decisions remain relevant when maintenance starts.
No routine percentage dose reductions: the team may hold or stop immunotherapy and treat the adverse effect.

Before requested restart, document whether any previous event met permanent-discontinuation criteria; absent history is not a negative history. Current recovery, steroid taper and consultant confirmation cannot override a prior permanent-stop event. The safety of reinitiating pembrolizumab after immune myocarditis is not established. Preserve the specific controlled-endocrine continuation exceptions.

context_profiles.regimen_role: Nivolumab and ipilimumab for advanced melanoma
context_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab and ipilimumab help immune cells recognise and attack melanoma. The combination phase is followed by nivolumab alone when appropriate. The aim in this setting is to control advanced disease; benefit and toxicity are reviewed for the individual.
context_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00431a: advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults. This patient guide is the melanoma context, not the separate liver-cancer indication.
context_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can reduce T-cell activity. This can help immune cells act against melanoma, but it can also allow inflammation in healthy organs. It is not conventional chemotherapy and side effects can occur even after doses have stopped. The four-dose combination phase has a different treatment plan from nivolumab maintenance.

If appropriate, nivolumab alone then continues on the team-selected two-weekly or four-weekly schedule, by the prescribed IV or subcutaneous route. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.

Four induction doses do not mean the whole treatment course is four doses.
Prior immune toxicity and permanent-stop decisions remain relevant when maintenance starts.

Abnormal liver tests or creatinine do not establish immune causality. Record clinician-assessed hepatitis/nephritis before the definitive source hold/stop pathway; unexplained abnormalities remain a clinical-review decision.

KEYNOTE-091 final OS analysis at ESMO 2026 did not demonstrate a statistically significant OS improvement; chemotherapy-subgroup DFS figures are updated and labelled separately from metastatic KEYNOTE-024.

Requested restart needs documented source-specific recovery, required steroid management/taper and consultant confirmation. Table 1 endocrine exceptions remain separate; existing 12-week failure/taper and permanent-stop criteria retain priority.

For pembrolizumab, grade 2 immune myocarditis, encephalitis or Guillain–Barré syndrome requires withholding and urgent specialist assessment; grades 3–4 require permanent discontinuation. EMA Table 1 separately addresses myocarditis–myositis–myasthenia gravis overlap: use the highest individual CTCAE v4.0 grade; hold grade 2 and permanently stop grades 3–4.

Before requested restart, document whether any previous event met permanent-discontinuation criteria; absent history is not a negative history. Current recovery, steroid taper and consultant confirmation cannot override a prior permanent-stop event. The safety of reinitiating pembrolizumab after immune myocarditis is not established. Preserve the specific controlled-endocrine continuation exceptions.

Shared-protocol eligibility audit now includes head-and-neck, adjuvant RCC, urothelial and cervical maintenance selection. These are distinct from the existing lung, colorectal and melanoma patient-service contexts.

context_profiles.regimen_role: Lung cancer only: first-line metastatic NSCLC or adjuvant NSCLC after surgery and platinum chemotherapy
context_profiles.clinical_summary: PD-1 blockade restores antitumour T-cell activity. First-line metastatic and post-resection adjuvant NSCLC have separate populations, treatment goals and evidence; the shared protocol does not make their eligibility interchangeable.
context_profiles.treatment_setting: Lung cancer only: first-line metastatic NSCLC or adjuvant NSCLC after surgery and platinum chemotherapy
context_profiles.component_rationale: Pembrolizumab: Pembrolizumab is an antibody that blocks PD-1, a control switch on immune T cells. Cancer cells can use this switch to reduce immune attack. Blocking it can help the immune system recognise and attack cancer. The same increased immune activity can inflame healthy organs, which is why new symptoms need attention even after treatment ends.
context_profiles.schedule_context: Pembrolizumab 400 mg is given as a drip over about 30 minutes on Day 1 every 6 weeks (42 days). The hospital visit is longer because of checks and preparation. After complete surgery and platinum chemotherapy, the adjuvant course lasts up to 12 months. For metastatic cancer, treatment continues while it remains helpful and tolerable; the team may consider stopping after 24 months of sustained response without progression, or continuing when appropriate.
key_points: Minimal emetic risk; no usual routine premedication.
No pembrolizumab dose reduction; apply specific hold/permanent-stop and restart criteria.
Grade 4/recurrent grade3 generic immune rules have specific endocrine exceptions; controlled hypothyroidism need not interrupt treatment.
Creatinine is ×ULN, never ×baseline; hepatitis and nephritis thresholds must not be confused with stable organ impairment recommendations.
Every-3–6-week thyroid checks continue on both infusion schedules.
Shared clinical protocol; new patient suite is lung-only.

Abnormal liver tests or creatinine do not establish immune causality. Record clinician-assessed hepatitis/nephritis before the definitive source hold/stop pathway; unexplained abnormalities remain a clinical-review decision.

KEYNOTE-091 final OS analysis at ESMO 2026 did not demonstrate a statistically significant OS improvement; chemotherapy-subgroup DFS figures are updated and labelled separately from metastatic KEYNOTE-024.

For pembrolizumab, grade 2 immune myocarditis, encephalitis or Guillain–Barré syndrome requires withholding and urgent specialist assessment; grades 3–4 require permanent discontinuation. EMA Table 1 separately addresses myocarditis–myositis–myasthenia gravis overlap: use the highest individual CTCAE v4.0 grade; hold grade 2 and permanently stop grades 3–4.

Before requested restart, document whether any previous event met permanent-discontinuation criteria; absent history is not a negative history. Current recovery, steroid taper and consultant confirmation cannot override a prior permanent-stop event. The safety of reinitiating pembrolizumab after immune myocarditis is not established. Preserve the specific controlled-endocrine continuation exceptions.

premedication_and_prophylaxis: Minimal emetic risk; routine antiemetic prophylaxis and routine infusion premedication are usually unnecessary; follow individual/local rescue plan.
Immune alert card, early reporting, appropriate contraception and specialist treatment of immune toxicities.
patient_education: Pembrolizumab alone has a minimal risk of causing sickness. Routine anti-sickness medicines or infusion premedicines are not usually needed; your team can prescribe symptom relief if required.
Carry your alert card during treatment and afterwards. Show it when seeking urgent care; symptoms can be mistaken for an infection or an ordinary stomach upset.
Some immune effects need steroids or hormone replacement. Follow the prescribed plan and do not stop steroids suddenly. Ask for help if symptoms worsen or you cannot take essential medicines.

Discuss pregnancy, fertility and breastfeeding before treatment. Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least four months after the last dose. If pregnancy is possible or occurs, contact your oncology team promptly.
special_support: No routine antiemetic prophylaxis or routine infusion premedication is usually required. Use an individual/local symptom-relief prescription if needed.
Carry the immunotherapy alert card and report possible immune symptoms promptly during and after treatment.
Blood count, renal/liver profile and glucose before each cycle; thyroid every 3–6 weeks, cortisol if clinically indicated.
Effective contraception during treatment and at least 4 months after the last dose.

baseline: Confirm the exact lung indication and treatment aim. Metastatic first-line: validated PD-L1 TPS ≥50%, no EGFR mutation or ALK translocation, stage IV, no prior systemic metastatic treatment, ECOG 0–1.

Adjuvant: complete resection, prior platinum chemotherapy, high recurrence-risk/pathological stage IB–IIIA AJCC7 source criteria, ECOG 0–1; confirm reimbursement/access separately. No metastatic TPS50 eligibility requirement applies.

FBC, renal and liver profiles, glucose and thyroid function. Review autoimmune disease, prior interstitial lung disease, infection, untreated brain metastases, steroid/immunosuppressive use, prior checkpoint treatment, pregnancy/breastfeeding and medicines.
before_each_cycle: Before each cycle: FBC, renal/liver profile and glucose; assess symptoms, immune toxicity and current medicines.
Check any new cough, breathlessness, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, rash, thirst/polyuria, fatigue, headache, weakness, chest pain or neurological change promptly; investigate alternative causes.
ongoing: Thyroid function every 3–6 weeks; on the 42-day schedule this is not every other cycle. Cortisol when clinically indicated, with sample timing and steroid context documented.
Disease imaging follows the supervising consultant plan. Clinically stable apparent early progression may need confirmation; do not automatically continue or stop without review.

Immune effects may persist or start after treatment ends. Maintain alert-card, urgent-contact and hormone-replacement follow-up; contraception during treatment and at least four months after the final dose.

If liver or kidney results deteriorate, investigate alternative causes and document immune attribution before permanent immune-toxicity discontinuation. Stable impairment and immune injury are different pathways.

During a treatment hold, record the original event and grade, recurrence, any permanent-stop criterion, current recovery and steroid/hormone plan before considering rechallenge. Controlled grade 2 adrenal/hypophysitis has a hormone-control review path; it is not automatic treatment clearance.
priority_toxicities: Immune inflammation of lungs, bowel, liver, kidneys, hormone glands, skin, heart and nervous system
Infusion reactions
Some effects need steroids, hospital care or long-term hormone replacement
Effects may start after the final dose
urgent_review_signals: Contact the oncology team immediately for new or worsening breathlessness, chest pain, persistent diarrhoea, severe tummy pain, yellow skin/eyes, much less urine, severe headache, marked weakness, confusion, unusual thirst or passing much more urine, or a spreading/blistering rash. For severe breathing difficulty, collapse, seizure or other immediately dangerous symptoms, seek emergency care. Do not wait for the next infusion.

Investigate combined muscle weakness/pain, visual symptoms, breathlessness, chest pain or dysrhythmia urgently; consider myocarditis–myositis–myasthenia overlap. Do not wait for all features or for the next infusion.

context_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab and ipilimumab help immune cells recognise and attack melanoma. The combination phase is followed by nivolumab alone when appropriate. The aim in this setting is to control advanced disease; benefit and toxicity are reviewed for the individual.
context_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00431a: advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults. This patient guide is the melanoma context, not the separate liver-cancer indication.
context_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can reduce T-cell activity. This can help immune cells act against melanoma, but it can also allow inflammation in healthy organs. It is not conventional chemotherapy and side effects can occur even after doses have stopped. Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another checkpoint involved in controlling T cells. Combining it with nivolumab increases immune activity and can increase immune-related toxicity. The four-dose combination phase has a different treatment plan from nivolumab maintenance.
context_profiles.schedule_context: The combination phase gives nivolumab followed by ipilimumab by IV infusion every three weeks for up to four doses. If appropriate, nivolumab alone then continues on the team-selected two-weekly or four-weekly schedule, by the prescribed IV or subcutaneous route. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.

context_profiles.regimen_role: Nivolumab and ipilimumab for advanced melanoma
context_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab and ipilimumab help immune cells recognise and attack melanoma. The combination phase is followed by nivolumab alone when appropriate. The aim in this setting is to control advanced disease; benefit and toxicity are reviewed for the individual.
context_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00431a: advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults. This patient guide is the melanoma context, not the separate liver-cancer indication.
context_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can reduce T-cell activity. This can help immune cells act against melanoma, but it can also allow inflammation in healthy organs. It is not conventional chemotherapy and side effects can occur even after doses have stopped. Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another checkpoint involved in controlling T cells. Combining it with nivolumab increases immune activity and can increase immune-related toxicity. The four-dose combination phase has a different treatment plan from nivolumab maintenance.
context_profiles.schedule_context: The combination phase gives nivolumab followed by ipilimumab by IV infusion every three weeks for up to four doses. If appropriate, nivolumab alone then continues on the team-selected two-weekly or four-weekly schedule, by the prescribed IV or subcutaneous route. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.
key_points: This is nivolumab1/ipilimumab3, not the lower-ipilimumab combination.
Four induction doses do not mean the whole treatment course is four doses.
Prior immune toxicity and permanent-stop decisions remain relevant when maintenance starts.
No routine percentage dose reductions: the team may hold or stop immunotherapy and treat the adverse effect.

For pembrolizumab, grade 2 immune myocarditis, encephalitis or Guillain–Barré syndrome requires withholding and urgent specialist assessment; grades 3–4 require permanent discontinuation. EMA Table 1 separately addresses myocarditis–myositis–myasthenia gravis overlap: use the highest individual CTCAE v4.0 grade; hold grade 2 and permanently stop grades 3–4.

Before requested restart, document whether any previous event met permanent-discontinuation criteria; absent history is not a negative history. Current recovery, steroid taper and consultant confirmation cannot override a prior permanent-stop event. The safety of reinitiating pembrolizumab after immune myocarditis is not established. Preserve the specific controlled-endocrine continuation exceptions.

Adjuvant RCC: adult clear-cell disease at increased recurrence risk after nephrectomy, with metastatic-lesion resection where applicable; ECOG 0–2; start within12weeks of surgery. The initiation window is not a recurring-cycle limit.

Urothelial: separate post-platinum progression and first-line cisplatin-ineligible pathways. Confirm source-appropriate histology/site and advanced setting. First-line requires validated CPS; NCCP indication table ≥10 conflicts with eligibility >10, so exact10 needs reconciliation. Do not impose this CPS threshold on the post-platinum pathway.

Cervical maintenance: adult persistent/recurrent/metastatic disease, induction chemotherapy completed, validated PD-L1 CPS ≥1 and ECOG 0–2. Do not confuse maintenance monotherapy with its induction combination.
